question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x={cosh}^{2}⁡x+{sinh}^{2}⁡x
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \int (\operatorname{cosh}⁡x(2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+1)+\operatorname{sinh}⁡x(2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & \,=\int (2{cosh}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+2{sinh}^{2}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & \,=\int (2({cosh}^{2}⁡x+{sinh}^{2}⁡x)+\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & \,=\int (2\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & \,=2\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+C \\  & \,=\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
